paragraphs: A day's work is very fragmented: screening resumes in the recruitment system and scheduling interviews in the morning, processing entry materials, signing contracts, and entering files in the afternoon; employees come to ask questions about social security and vacation at any time, and they have to answer them one by one; at the end of the month, they check attendance and compile reports. During the peak recruitment season, there are a huge amount of resumes. The smarter the system, the more assistants are required to "use tools to manage the process."

The preliminary screening of resumes and mass notification are handed over to AI. Where is the position of the HR assistant? Answer: At the fork in the road of transformation.

Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) show that there will be approximately 95,200 human resources assistants on the job in 2024, which is expected to rise to 88,400 by 2034. There will be a net loss of approximately 6,800 positions, with an average annual vacancy of approximately 9,000, and the median annual salary in 2026 will be approximately US$49,400 (BLS OOH, 2026).

The impact of AI on human resources assistants is the "most typical category": resume screening, interview notifications, attendance statistics, and table sorting--these tasks that take up most of the assistant's time are quickly taken over by AI and HR systems. Positions will not be cleared overnight, but the number of assistant positions will continue to be reduced, leaving only the "human flesh and blood" parts: abnormal case handling, employee emotional communication, and cross-department coordination. If you don’t want to be replaced, you have to go to a specialist position with judgment.

paragraphs: 6/10 shows that the core actions of this industry - screening, statistics, and sorting - are exactly the areas where AI is best at, and they belong to professions with "clear alternative paths".

Medium and high exposure means high risk: if you stay at the transaction execution level, there is a high probability of being replaced by HR systems and AI. But think about it conversely, the system does the chores for you, which just saves time for transformation - taking the human resources certificate, learning about salary and performance, taking on recruitment projects, upgrading from "processing" to "making judgments", only then can the value of the position be preserved.

Learning human resource management requires two legs: "methods + tools": you need to understand the six modules, but also data analysis and AI tools. Don't expect to work as an assistant for a lifetime. You have planned to become a specialist or BP since your freshman year. Internships are more important than endorsements.

Start the transition now: choose one specialty, such as recruiting, employee relations, or compensation and performance, and become proficient with HR systems and AI tools. Earn an HR credential and take ownership of projects so your resume shows results, not just completed tasks.

The assistant position is suitable as a springboard to enter the HR industry, but there must be a clear upgrade plan. When applying for a job, emphasize which HR systems and data analysis tools you can use. Being able to independently run through the entire recruitment or onboarding and exit process is more competitive than general "administrative personnel experience."

Don’t recruit assistants as “system operators”. AI can already replace most of the operations. Recruit people who are willing to learn and can grow into specialists, and provide supporting training and promotion channels - an assistant who can handle recruitment projects is worth several times more than an ordinary operator.
